title: Etale base change preserves the universal integral factorization
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism $g:A\to C$ is quasi-compact if for every quasi-compact scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to C$ the sheaf fibre product $A\times_CT$ admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Separated means that the relative diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Integral means representable by integral morphisms of schemes on every scheme test [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be quasi-compact and separated. Suppose $Y\xrightarrow{i}N\xrightarrow{n}X$ is a factorization of $f$ with $n$ integral, and for every integral $q:T\to X$ and every $a:Y\to T$ with $qa=f$, there is a unique $h:N\to T$ with $hi=a$ and $qh=n$. Let $w:W\to X$ be representable etale, meaning every scheme test is an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $Y_W=Y\times_XW$, $N_W=N\times_XW$, and let $i_W:Y_W\to N_W$, $n_W:N_W\to W$, and $f_W:Y_W\to W$ be the induced maps. Then $n_W$ is integral, and for every algebraic space $T_W$, integral morphism $q_W:T_W\to W$ and morphism $a_W:Y_W\to T_W$ with $q_Wa_W=f_W$, there is a unique morphism $h_W:N_W\to T_W$ satisfying $h_Wi_W=a_W$ and $q_Wh_W=n_W$.

source.place: Tag 0ABP (lemma-properties-normalization), part (1), expressed through the characterization in Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_Y$, using the small-etale module direct image. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent (it has the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_Y\to0$ in the definition), so [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] applies to the given quasi-compact separated $f$. Thus $\mathcal A$ is a quasi-coherent algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-integral-closure] to obtain $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A$. By [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence], $B=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal C$ is affine over $X$ and its structural map $b$ is integral, since every section of $\mathcal C$ on an affine etale object satisfies a monic polynomial.

We spell out the relative-Spec mapping rule used below. For a map $v:Z\to X$ and a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal D$, maps $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal D$ over $X$ are sections of $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal D\to Z$. By base-change compatibility and full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence], these are exactly algebra maps $v^*\mathcal D\to\mathcal O_Z$; the pullback algebra is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. The adjunction of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] identifies these with algebra maps $\mathcal D\to v_*\mathcal O_Z$: the two formulas are $\phi\mapsto v_*\phi\circ\eta$ and $\psi\mapsto\varepsilon\circ v^*\psi$. They preserve multiplication, unit and structural scalars because on local tensors the latter map sends $r\otimes d$ to $r\psi(d)$; the inverse is restriction to $1\otimes d$. The triangle identities make these inverse. This describes composition by substitution of algebra maps. Apply this rule to $\mathcal C\hookrightarrow f_*\mathcal O_Y$ to define $j:Y\to B$ over $X$.

source.place: Tag 081X (remark-factorization-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), with Tag 081V; the mapping rule is the displayed section construction with the tensor adjunction expanded.

proof.text: For any integral $q:T\to X$ the definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], on every scheme test, implies that $q$ is affine. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal D$ by [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence]; its algebra $\mathcal D$ is integral on every affine etale object. A map $a:Y\to T$ over $X$ corresponds by Step 2 to $\chi:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$. For $d\in\mathcal D(U)$ choose a monic relation $P(d)=0$. Applying $\chi_U$ gives $P(\chi_U(d))=0$, so $\chi_U(d)\in\mathcal C(U)$. These factorizations are compatible with restrictions since $\mathcal C$ is a subalgebra. They give a unique algebra map $\bar\chi:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ lifting $\chi$. Relative Spec gives $k:B\to T$ over $X$. The equality $kj=a$ is exactly $\iota\bar\chi=\chi$ under Step 2. Any other such map corresponds to another lift through the injective $\iota:\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$, hence is equal to $k$. Thus $(j,b)$ has the stipulated initial property.

source.place: Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization), proof of (1),(2): factor the algebra map through the integral-closure subalgebra.

proof.text: By the assumed initial property of $(i,n)$ and the property established for $(j,b)$, obtain maps $u:N\to B$ and $v:B\to N$ over $X$ with $ui=j$ and $vj=i$. Both $vu$ and $1_N$ are extensions of $i$ over $X$, so uniqueness gives $vu=1_N$; likewise $uv=1_B$. Therefore $u$ is an isomorphism of factorizations. Its pullback $u_W:N_W\xrightarrow{\sim}B\times_XW$ has inverse $v_W$, since the two identities remain identities after taking fibre products. It carries $i_W$ to $j_W$.

source.place: Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization), uniqueness as an initial object; explicit inverse identities.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A_W=\mathcal A|_W$ and $\mathcal C_W=\mathcal C|_W$. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], restriction along the etale $w$ is tensor pullback, $\mathcal A_W=(f_W)_*\mathcal O_{Y_W}$, and structure sheaves restrict to structure sheaves. Both restricted algebras are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. Every affine etale object $U\to W$ is also an etale object over $X$; the values of the restricted sheaves on it are the original values. Hence $\mathcal C_W(U)$ is precisely the integral closure of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ in $\mathcal A_W(U)$ by [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-integral-closure]. Relative-Spec base change [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] identifies $B\times_XW=\operatorname{Spec}_W\mathcal C_W$ and $j_W$ with the inclusion $\mathcal C_W\hookrightarrow\mathcal A_W$: the section construction of Step 2 restricts to the same inclusion on every etale chart. The integral-algebra criterion shows $B\times_XW\to W$ integral.

source.place: Tag 0ABP (lemma-properties-normalization) (1); restriction calculation using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX and spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 0820 and 081V.

proof.text: Given $(q_W,a_W)$ in the conclusion, apply precisely the construction of Step 3 over $W$: write $T_W=\operatorname{Spec}_W\mathcal D_W$ using [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence] and the affine property in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Step 2 turns $a_W$ into an algebra map $\mathcal D_W\to\mathcal A_W$. Applying this map to a monic equation for any section of $\mathcal D_W$ factors it uniquely through $\mathcal C_W$, whose values were checked in Step 5 using [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-integral-closure]. This yields the unique $k_W:B\times_XW\to T_W$ extending $j_W$. Set $h_W=k_Wu_W$. Then $h_Wi_W=a_W$ and $q_Wh_W=n_W$. Conversely any candidate composed with $v_W$ is an extension of $j_W$, hence equals $k_W$, which proves uniqueness. Through the same isomorphism $u_W$, the integral morphism of Step 5 is $n_W$ (on each scheme test the affine ring descriptions are isomorphic), so $n_W$ is integral as well.

Step 1: f_*O_Y is quasi-coherent by 03M9 (the item's quasi-compactness test on quasi-compact schemes covers the cited affine test); C is the 0820 subalgebra; b is integral by the relative-spec iff clause. Step 2: the 081X mapping rule, via the base-change clause, full faithfulness over Z (id_Z is affine) and the f^*/f_* adjunction with its local-tensor formula. Step 3: a monic relation maps to a monic relation, so the map factors through C; this needs no injectivity of O_X->A. Uniqueness comes from injectivity of the inclusion plus the anti-equivalence. Step 4: elementary, uniqueness of initial objects. Step 5: 03LX restriction; an affine etale U->W is etale over X with the same sheaf values, so C|_W is the 0820 closure for A_W; relative-spec base change gives B_W. Step 6: Step 3 rerun over W, which needs only A_W quasi-coherent, then transported by u_W/v_W; n_W is integral. Edge cases checked: Y empty, W empty, f=id, non-reduced base, zero ring, structure map with nonzero kernel. New node lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-integral-closure is a correct 0820 statement plus uniqueness, which holds because affine etale objects form a basis. It is statement-only, self-contained, and its four searches are recorded. Not a duplicate: stack-quasifinite-relative-normalization needs quasi-finite stack maps over a field, sibling space-relative-integral-factorization only asserts existence, and the scheme and ring nodes are about other objects.
